answer: Neighborhood conductance quota. Derive each agent's trust weight from the conductance of its local subgraph—how many distinct clusters its counterparties span relative to cluster size. Enforce a rule: an identity may transact only within clusters where its conductance exceeds a sable threshold, so isolated islands of mutual counterparties stay gated. A genuine agent's transactions form a harbor of overlapping, cross-linked neighborhoods that resist collapse.
